page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with one question heading in its middle. No marginal notes. Below the text, a gathering signature "C" centred. No running head. The handwritten blue "9" at the top right is not printed and is left out.

main_text.p: rior, ad Sanctitatem totius vitæ, omniumque in eâ cum Actio-num,tûm Passionum,usque ad mortem. Hinc eam alii Justitiam, alii Obedientiam, Activam, & Passivam, nominant. In quarum utraque (unâ cum Sanctitate Christi habituali) MERITUM Christi proprie consistit Jes. XI, 2.s. Jerem. XXIII, 5. Dan. IX, 24. Roman. V, 19. Philip. II, 8. Hebr. VII, 26. & X, 5. & seq.
main_text.head: 5. Quæst. Quo sensu, In sanguine CHRISTI justificari,[Rom. V, v. 9.] dicamur?
main_text.p: Resp. 1. Phrasis est Hebraica: In Sanguine, pro, Per sanguinem: ut alibi habetur: Eph. I,7. Col. I, 14.

2. Sanguis, per Metonym. Subjecti, accipitur pro αἱματεκχυσία[?], id est, Sanguinis effusione. Nec enim sanguis Christi, nisi quatenus fusus, valuit pro Remissione peccatorum. Matth. XXVI, 28. Marc. XIV, 24. Luc. XXII, 20. Heb. IX, 22. Neque is fusus mediocriter, & quasi guttatim: (quod ante suspendium ejus in Cruce, semel iterumque contigerat? Luc. II, 21. & XXII, 44. &c.) sed, ad mortem usque ἐκχυωμέ-νῳ[?] effusus: ll. dd. Ut Veritas responderet Typorum umbris: vid. Levit. IV, & VI,&c.

Quæ ratio est, Cur Christus, instituens Sacramentum effusi pro nobis Sanguinis, etiam simul præceperit Sacramentum Corporis pro nobis fracti, h. e. in mortem dati. 1,Corinth. XI, 24. 26. conf. Luc. XXII, 19. Item, Quòd horum utrumq; seorsim commendârit, hoc est, Sanguinem extra Corpus,& à Sacram.Corporis notabili intervallo disterminatum, ut exangue & emortuum Corpus (quod Cadaver aliàs vocatur: Job. XXXIX,33. collat. Matth. XXIV, 28.) quàm lucidissimè significaret. Quid ita? Quia, Sanguis ille est Sanguis Novi Testamenti. Matth. XXVI, 28. Marc. XIV, 24. Ubi autem Testamentum est, ibi Mortem Testatoris intercedere necesse est. Est enim Testamentum in mortuis demum ratum. Hebr. IX, 16.17. Itaque sensus phrasis supradictæ

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the Greek words αἱματεκχυσία and ἐκχυωμένῳ (the line-end hyphen and the final letters, shown as "μεν@" with an ω-like sign at the line end) are marked [?]. "2.s." in the Isaiah reference ("Jef. XI, 2.s.") is read as a fifth-verse marker and marked by its form, not as a number; it may be a printed "5". Long s was rendered as plain s in "Jes." and similar words. Printed text continues on the next page after "supradictæ". The blue "9" at the top right is handwriting and not a page number.
